headline: Medium risk: RD-Agent’s API-heavy research workflow can leak or cascade outputs, while Authelia’s auth role limits direct conflict but not pairwise misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, but no browser or subprocess execution is documented. RD-Agent runs browsers and consumes external content via APIs, so a prompt-injection bridge is plausible only through manual or file-based handoff, not a default shared channel. The pairwise pathway exists but is constrained.
conditions: IF outputs from RD-Agent are copied into Authelia configuration or policy text
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is used to move browser-derived content into Authelia
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted RD-Agent outputs into auth policy files
Review any forwarded headers or OIDC claims before deployment
Use separate workspaces for research artifacts and auth configs
Add a short human review step before applying Authelia changes

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly touches logs, execution traces, competition datasets, and financial reports, and it sends data to external model APIs. Authelia handles OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, so if the pair shares a workspace or auth context, sensitive material can flow from RD-Agent into Authelia-adjacent outputs or upstream services. The default risk is data exposure, not proven exfiltration.
conditions: IF RD-Agent logs or datasets are placed in a directory Authelia can read
IF Authelia forwards request metadata derived from RD-Agent-controlled inputs to an upstream IdP
mitigations: Keep RD-Agent logs and datasets on a separate volume
Redact secrets from logs before any forwarding step
Restrict Authelia access to only its config directory
Rotate any API keys used by RD-Agent if shared storage is detected

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress but no filesystem write or subprocess capability is documented, while RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because the orchestrator and filesystem layout are not specified.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same log or config directory
IF an external orchestrator grants both write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign distinct directories for each agent
Run each agent under a separate OS user
Avoid shared git working trees
Check for accidental overlap in mounted volumes

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is a research automation system that can generate outputs from papers, datasets, and traces, and Authelia can consume configuration and identity-related inputs. If RD-Agent-produced text is treated as authoritative and then fed into auth policy or forwarding rules, errors can cascade into incorrect access decisions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF RD-Agent outputs are used to draft Authelia policy or OIDC settings without review
IF Authelia is configured to trust RD-Agent-generated claims or metadata
mitigations: Require manual review of any RD-Agent-generated config text
Validate auth rules against a known-good test case
Keep research outputs out of production auth pipelines
Add a second reviewer for changes touching identity policy

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and research papers, which can carry residency or retention obligations. Authelia is an authentication service with OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, so if it processes the same identity-linked data, policy mismatches can arise. No single residency violation is proven, but the compliance surface is real.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated logs are routed through RD-Agent and then into Authelia-managed identity flows
IF retention settings differ between RD-Agent logs and Authelia audit records
mitigations: Document which data classes each agent may process
Set a short retention window for RD-Agent logs
Verify Authelia audit-log retention separately
Exclude regulated datasets from research runs unless approved
